editorNote: A day built on what we could read in full: a reported $35 billion Chinese order for Nvidia cards that Nvidia may not be able to fill, a Swiss ETF approval, Rocket Lab's rebound and gold's slide. Facts only; no view on direction is offered.

stories.headline: ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent reportedly order over $35 billion of Nvidia RTX PRO 5500 cards, but supply may fall far short
stories.summary: Reuters, citing sources, reports the three firms ordered more than 3 million of the export-compliant cards at about $11,400 each, mainly for AI inference. Total Chinese orders reportedly exceed 6 million, and Nvidia has told partners some may receive only 5% to 10% of what they asked for.
stories.whyItMatters: The report puts a number on Alibaba's AI compute demand and on the supply limit; early samples are expected in December and commercial deliveries in Q1 2027.

sourceLinks.title: Exclusive: ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent place over $35 billion worth of Nvidia chip orders (Reuters via WSAU)

stories.headline: Rocket Lab rises 3.9% pre-market after a 20%-plus slide; Q3 results are set for Nov. 9
stories.summary: Shares were up 3.9% to $52.87 before the open on Oct. 21, after falling more than 20% between Oct. 13 and 20 when Neutron's debut was pushed to 2027. Rocket Lab will report Q3 results on Nov. 9 after the close, and Iridium shareholders approved its roughly $8 billion acquisition bid with 99.6% of votes cast.
stories.whyItMatters: The Iridium deal still depends on remaining conditions and approvals; Yahoo Finance says it cannot tell how much of the move came from the broader market, which was up.

sourceLinks.title: Why Is Rocket Lab Stock Rising in Pre-Market Trading? - Yahoo Finance

stories.headline: Switzerland's FINMA approves a first spot bitcoin ETF for retail investors, with the usual diversification rules waived
stories.summary: FINMA announced on Oct. 20 that it classifies the fund as an 'other fund for alternative investments' and waived diversification requirements, citing bitcoin's longer trading history and higher volumes than other cryptocurrencies. Providers must mitigate custody and operational risks, and Financial Services Act conduct rules apply to sales.
stories.whyItMatters: FINMA declined to name the fund or issuer, and the report gives no launch date.

sourceLinks.title: Swiss regulator FINMA approves country's first spot bitcoin ETF for retail investors - The Block

stories.headline: Gold trades near $4,122 after three straight daily losses as rate-hike bets build
stories.summary: FXStreet reports spot gold fell about 0.43% on Tuesday even as Treasury yields and the dollar weakened. Markets price about a 14% chance of a Fed hike in October and nearly 90% for December, per Prime Terminal, and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh holds a press conference on Oct. 28.
stories.whyItMatters: Analysts cited in the piece list $4,100 as support (a break targets the Oct. 14 low at $4,073) and $4,200 as resistance.

sourceLinks.title: Gold struggles near $4,150 as global rate hike risks loom - FXStreet (via Mitrade)
